audit.title: Migrating from VRF v1
audit.summary: This is a task-oriented VRF migration guide with strong inline references to canonical Solidity contracts (11 primary-source links) and good concrete numerics (3–200 block confirmations, up to 100 addresses, the Nov 29 2024 cutover). Its single biggest GEO weakness is a **scope/entity confusion**: the page is titled "Migrating from VRF v1" but the "Update your code" section instructs removing **v2** imports (`VRFConsumerBaseV2`) — mixing two distinct migration paths, which muddies entity resolution and retrieval. The highest-lift opportunity is a top-of-page **v1→v2.5 API mapping table** (the page has zero tables) that engines can lift verbatim. Metadata is entirely absent (no JSON-LD, canonical, or dates), and the Solidity snippets are embedded in MDX `Tabs`/`Fragment` components — the deterministic scan detected **0 fenced code blocks**, a real risk that agents won't extract the code at all.

recommendations.title: Add a v1→v2.5 API mapping table at the top
recommendations.where: directly under "Comparing VRF v1 to VRF v2.5"
recommendations.issue: page has 0 tables; core renames are buried in numbered steps.
recommendations.change: add a 3-column table — *v1 → v2.5 → notes* — with rows for `VRFConsumerBase`→`VRFConsumerBaseV2Plus`, `requestRandomness`→`requestRandomWords`, `fulfillRandomness`→`fulfillRandomWords` (returns `uint256[]`), single→multi-word, and the new `extraArgs`/`nativePayment` parameter.
recommendations.why: a self-contained mapping table is the single most liftable artifact for "how do I migrate VRF v1 to v2.5" queries.

recommendations.title: Resolve the v1-vs-v2 scope confusion
recommendations.issue: "remove the v2 `VRFConsumerBaseV2` import" on a page titled *Migrating from VRF v1*.
recommendations.change: either explicitly state the "Update your code" section serves both v1 and v2 sources ("If migrating from v1, remove `VRFConsumerBase`; if from v2, remove `VRFConsumerBaseV2`"), or split into clearly labeled v1 and v2 subsections.
recommendations.why: mixed source-version instructions cause engines to synthesize wrong migration steps; disambiguation prevents inverted/confused answers.

recommendations.title: Add symptom/query-phrased headings
recommendations.where: new H3s or a short FAQ near the end
recommendations.issue: no entries matching "what changed in VRF v2.5", or the compile error from the removed base contract.
recommendations.change: add headings such as "What's different between VRF v1 and v2.5?" and a troubleshooting note for `fulfillRandomWords` signature mismatch (memory vs calldata across `@chainlink/contracts` 1.1.0/1.1.1).
recommendations.why: devs query by symptom and question, not by "Comparing…" — these win retrieval the current concept-titled prose loses.

recommendations.title: Add TechArticle JSON-LD, canonical, and a visible last-updated date
recommendations.issue: measured 0 JSON-LD, canonical MISSING, no dateModified.
recommendations.change: emit `TechArticle` JSON-LD with `dateModified`, `about: "Chainlink VRF v2.5"`, and a canonical URL; surface "Last updated" on-page.
recommendations.why: freshness and structured metadata raise parseability and trust for a version-migration doc.

recommendations.title: Ensure code blocks render as real fenced blocks
recommendations.issue: deterministic scan detected 0 fenced blocks despite visible code.
recommendations.change: verify the served HTML emits `<pre><code class="language-solidity">`; if MDX components strip fencing, add a plain fallback or ensure the `.md` endpoint preserves fences.
recommendations.why: agents extract labeled fenced code; if the fences are lost, the copy-pasteable migration code is invisible to them.

recommendations.title: Replace vague quantifiers with numbers
recommendations.change: state the parameter count added to `requestRandomWords`, and either cite a representative premium % or link the exact figure with "(e.g. X% on Ethereum mainnet)."
recommendations.why: quantified claims are among the highest-lift changes for citation.

antiPatterns: Scope/entity ambiguity: title references v1 while body instructs removing v2 imports.
Vague quantifiers: "several," "many," "low latency," "percentage-based" without a number.
Undated content on a time-sensitive migration topic (no visible last-updated).
Code fragments without imports/full-contract context (mitigated by Remix links).
offPageNotes: `llms.txt` is already referenced at the top — good site-level signal; confirm this page is listed in it.
Site-level JSON-LD/canonical templating likely governs the missing metadata; fix at the docs framework layer, not just this page.
Freshness cadence: a migration doc tied to the Nov 29 2024 cutover should carry a maintained `dateModified` sourced from the CMS.
